name: Dykes Landing on the Ocmulgee
unique: A landing inside the Ocmulgee Wildlife Management Area with two concrete ramps, canoe steps and riverside campsites, one of the stops on a water trail that runs from Macon to the coast.
buzz: Free camping on a river with a ramp is rare and locals guard it. Bring a licence for the fishing and everything you need for the night.

name: Ocmulgee Public Fishing Area
unique: A 106 acre lake stocked with bass, bluegill, crappie and catfish, with a pier, a boat ramp and a cleaning station, built for people who want to fish without owning a boat.
buzz: The pier and the bank fishing are the point, and the lake is small enough to learn. Alligators mean you keep your catch off the bank.

name: Bleckley County Courthouse and Cochran Historic District
unique: A 1913 courthouse with a 1928 school and a 1942 municipal building around it, a small New Deal era downtown that has held together better than most in middle Georgia.
buzz: A quiet hour on foot with the school and the municipal building worth a look. Five minutes off the highway.

name: Big Pig Jig
unique: One of the oldest and largest barbecue contests in the Southeast, with teams cooking whole hogs overnight and a sanctioned competition that has sent cooks to the national championships.
buzz: The overnight cook is the real event and the public walks the pits on Friday night. Get there before the judging starts Saturday.

name: Vienna Murals
unique: A mural series that started in 2004 and now covers downtown walls with scenes of Vienna in the 1930s and 1950s, down to a drugstore soda fountain and its cherry coke.
buzz: The soda fountain mural is the favourite, with the story of the drink named for the social services office next door. Easy walk from the courthouse.

name: Dooly County Courthouse
unique: A domed courthouse on a square in a county that once included most of this part of the state before it was carved into six others.
buzz: The square is the best block in town and the courthouse is the reason. Pair it with the murals and the cemetery walk.

name: Martin Luther King Jr Monument Park
unique: A downtown park built around a monument to King and the local movement, with plaques on the marches and the people who organized them in a middle Georgia mill town.
buzz: Small and well done, and the local names are what make it. Worth twenty minutes on a downtown walk.

name: Martin Movie House
unique: A downtown theatre running first run films, concerts and live shows in a restored house on the main street, part of a small chain of family owned cinemas.
buzz: Tickets are cheap and the room is warm. It has become the evening plan for downtown Dublin.

name: Beaverdam Wildlife Management Area
unique: Five and a half thousand acres of Oconee River bottomland with cypress sloughs, dove fields and a boat ramp, managed for quail and turkey.
buzz: Birders work the bottomland edges in spring. It is a working management area with seasons, so check the calendar.

name: A.B. Lee's Meat Market
customer: Cooks, hunters, locals stocking a freezer
unique: A butcher shop that cut its reputation on whole hog sausage and cured meat in a town where people still buy a quarter of a cow at a time.
buzz: The sausage is the local standard and the counter will tell you how to cook it. Cash and carry, and it gets busy before holidays.

name: Oconee River at Dublin
unique: A river with public landings above and below town and a greenway along the bank, where the current is easy and the shoals give a beginner something to read.
buzz: Flatwater with a few shoals and good access. Locals fish the bluff holes for shoal bass.

name: Traditions Highway 15
unique: A designated heritage route down Highway 15 through the pine and cotton counties of middle Georgia, with farm stands, sawmill towns and markers on the turpentine and wiregrass economy.
buzz: A drive rather than a destination, best in autumn when the cotton is in. The small town squares along it are the stops.

name: Wrightsville Downtown
unique: A crossroads town where three highways meet at a courthouse square, incorporated in 1866 and still built around the same block.
buzz: Quiet and unspoiled, with a couple of businesses that have lasted decades. Twenty minutes and you have seen it.

name: Johnson County Farm and Timber Country
unique: Pine plantation, peanut fields and deer woods on the edge of the Ohoopee sandhills, with hunting clubs and farm stands at the crossings.
buzz: Deer season is the busy time here. The Ohoopee dunes to the south are the odd landscape worth a detour.

name: Montgomery County Historic Village
unique: A collection of moved in log cabins, a church and a schoolhouse assembled on the Brewton-Parker College campus to show how this county lived before the railroad.
buzz: Small and free and easy to walk in half an hour. The college connection keeps it maintained.

name: Warren C. Crawley Sr Monument
customer: Civil rights travellers, local history people
unique: A monument to a Montgomery County educator and community leader, one of the few public markers in this part of Georgia to a Black local figure.
buzz: A quiet stop that raises questions about who gets remembered. Best paired with the historic village on the same trip.

name: Mount Vernon Square and Courthouse
unique: A courthouse square in a county created in 1793, one of the oldest in this part of the state, with the town laid out around it and the railroad a mile away.
buzz: The town is small and the square is the whole of it. A five minute stop on the way to Vidalia or Soperton.

name: Million Pines Arts and Crafts Festival
unique: A craft fair in the pine woods county that calls itself the million pines, with woodwork, quilts, cane syrup and the kind of vendors who make what they sell.
buzz: The woodwork and the syrup are the things to buy. Parking is in a field and the crowd is local.

name: Soperton Courthouse Square
unique: The square of Georgia's second smallest county by population, a railroad town named for a colonial governor's family and built on turpentine and timber.
buzz: Small, tidy and quick. The county history is mostly timber and the buildings show it.

name: Treutlen County Pine Woods
unique: County roads running through managed pine and hardwood creek bottoms where bobwhite and kestrels still hold on, between the Oconee and the Ocmulgee watersheds.
buzz: Early morning in spring is the time, and the roads are empty. Bring a map because the phone will give up.

name: Wheeler County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse in a county created in 1912 and named for a Confederate general, sitting where three rivers frame the land and the towns are named Alamo and Glenwood.
buzz: One of the smallest county seats in the state, and the building is the tallest thing in town. Two minutes off the highway.

name: Alligator Creek Wildlife Management Area
unique: Bottomland hardwood and creek swamp between the Little Ocmulgee and the Oconee, managed for deer, turkey and small game with the water table dictating where you can walk.
buzz: Quiet public land with very little pressure. Wear boots and check the season calendar before going.

name: Three Rivers Country
unique: A county framed by the Little Ocmulgee, the Oconee and the Ocmulgee, with landings on all three and water that changes character from creek to river within a mile.
buzz: Paddlers use it as a link between longer runs. Ramps are basic and the shoals are the interesting part.

name: Geographic Center of Georgia
unique: The marker for the geographic center of Georgia, out in the pine woods of Twiggs County, which means every direction from here is downhill in a sense.
buzz: A photo and a fact for the road. There is nothing else there, which is part of the charm.

name: Twiggs County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse in a county named for a Revolutionary general who never set foot in it, on land that was Creek and then cotton and now mostly pine.
buzz: The town is a crossroads and the courthouse is the landmark. Quick stop on the way to Macon.

name: Ocmulgee River at Twiggs
unique: The Ocmulgee forms the county's western line, with sandbars, cypress and bottomland hardwood that flood every winter and hold deer and hogs the rest of the year.
buzz: A quiet stretch of the water trail with almost no traffic. Water levels decide whether the sandbars are campsites or underfoot.
